editorial.summary: A live Oahu episode documenting DVDASA's move from a downtown studio to a ticketed room, its cast-origin story, David Choe's Hawaii rehab claim, his mother's late-starting daily painting practice, his rejection by Korean galleries, and his proposal for a voluntary distraction-free art residency modeled on the productive constraint he experienced in jail. The room also exposes the limits of transcript-only processing: music becomes repeated nonsense, applause was deleted as degeneration, audience identities are attached to family and sexual disclosures, and consent is repeatedly inverted for laughs. The public edition restores room reactions, labels music as untranscribable pending listening, protects attendees and nonparticipants, rejects transphobic framing and the phrase 'no means yes,' and preserves the episode's own crucial distinction between consensual adult sex work and trafficking. Dolphin-assisted therapy is retained as a first-person rehab claim, not validated medicine. CDC and FDA guidance replaces blanket claims about implants and breastfeeding with individualized evidence. Named dialogue remains withheld.
editorial.speaker_policy: UNKNOWN by default. Five coarse legacy windows and zero deliberately unrequested turns cannot support names. Live-stage visibility may help future labeling, but only an independently held-out voice test can authorize named dialogue.
sensitivity: Seven broad public-reader redactions protect a minor, an airline passenger, attendees, partners, children and intimate audience disclosures.
Live music and repeated vocal fragments are never guessed into lyrics.
The 17 removed audience cheers should be restored or represented as room reaction.
Health, consent, trafficking and allegation corrections remain editorial annotations rather than silent dialogue rewrites.
source_notes: The cleaner removed 820 empty artifacts and 117 degenerate runs totaling 39 seconds.
Seventeen genuine audience cheers at 170.68–197.76 were misclassified and require restoration or an `[audience cheers]` event.
Repeated `god`/`count` sequences in music regions at 82.20–82.58, 295.46–355.36 and 5392.88–5420.90 require audio review; they are not accepted as lyrics.
A review of dolphin-assisted therapy studies found major methodological limitations that prevent valid strong efficacy conclusions: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3420785/

CDC says many people with prior breast surgery can produce milk, but supply may be reduced depending on ducts, nerves, incision and implant placement: https://www.cdc.gov/breastfeeding-special-circumstances/hcp/illnesses-conditions/breast-surgery.html

FDA says some people with augmentation can breastfeed and some cannot; pregnancy itself can change breast shape and implants are not lifetime devices: https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/breast-implants/risks-and-complications-breast-implants

UNODC's consent issue paper supports keeping consensual adult sex work analytically distinct from trafficking while recognizing that coercion or abuse can make apparent consent irrelevant: https://www.unodc.org/documents/human-trafficking/2014/UNODC_2014_Issue_Paper_Consent.pdf
